#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit mu…

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --
  UNFORMATTED=$(dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed $STAGED_DART 2>/dev/null | grep '^Changed' || true)
  if [ -n "$UNFORMATTED" ]; then
    echo "❌ dart format could not fix these files (syntax error?):"
    echo "$UNFORMATTED"
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# THE shared fast gate (same script, same path filters as CI). --hook makes
# it derive the scope from the STAGED diff. It unsets GIT_* env itself
# after reading hook mode.
bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --hook

# Issue #447: crap4dart quality gates over the STAGED core diff
# (core-only #433 split — the flutter_app gates run in CI's
# app-crap-gate job). The root crap4dart.yaml enables exactly
# broken_goldens; `check --staged` no-ops when no Dart file is staged.
# Equivalent to the managed block `crap4dart install --force` would
# append — do not stack both. Requires crap4dart >= 0.9 (the gate
# framework; older pins only knew `analyze`).
if command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  C4D_VER=$(dart pub global list 2>/dev/null | awk '$1=="crap4dart"{print $2}')
  case "$C4D_VER" in
    # gh-1106: floor 0.11.0 — the root crap4dart.yaml duplication block
    # uses 0.11.0-only keys (ignore_locals/ignorable); the strict config
    # parser throws ConfigException on unknown keys, so older pins fail
    # rather than silently run without Type-2 detection.
    0.1[1-9].*|0.[2-9][0-9].*|[1-9].*)
      echo "🧪 crap4dart gates (staged core files)..."
      # gh-1106: --baseline — the Type-2 duplication gate ships with a
      # committed snapshot of pre-existing findings; hooks must flag only
      # NEW duplication, same contract as CI.
      if ! dart pub global run crap4dart check --staged --baseline; then
        echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — crap4dart gates" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      # Issue #1234 rework: the ≤2800 ceiling over test/ + example/ via
      # the loc-scope companion config (the package config's sources are
      # [lib, bin]; 0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override). No-ops
      # unless a staged file lives under test/ or example/.
      if ! dart pub global run crap4dart check --staged --config crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml --only loc; then
        echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — loc scope (test/example)" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      ;;
    "")
      ;; # not activated — skip silently (CI and the fast gate cover it)
    *)
      echo "⚠️  crap4dart $C4D_VER is too old for the gates (need >= 0.11.0);" \
           "skipping — run: dart pub global activate crap4dart '>=0.11.0 <0.12.0'" >&2
      ;;
  esac
fi

# Golden-coverage quick check — only when the staged diff can affect the
# flutter_app (the gate's own markers already told us the flutter stage
# ran or was skipped; recompute cheaply from the staged paths here).
STAGED=$(git diff --cached --name-only || true)
if echo "$STAGED" | grep -qE '^(flutter_app/|packages/|lib/|scripts/|\.github/|pubspec\.)' \
   || ! echo "$STAGED" | grep -qE '\.(md)$|^docs/|^prompts/'; then
  if command -v flutter >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "🔍 Checking golden coverage..."
    if python3 scripts/check_goldens.py --quick; then
      echo "✅ Golden gate OK"
    else
      exit 1
    fi
  fi
fi

# Issue #433 AC1 (cheap, config-only): README CRAP badge must equal the
# crap4dart.yaml thresholds — runs only when a config or the README is
# staged, i.e. exactly the files that can drift apart.
if echo "$STAGED" | grep -qE '(^|/)crap4dart\.yaml$|^README\.md$'; then
  python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py
fi

echo ""
echo "╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗"
echo "║  ✅ ALL QUALITY GATES PASSED — COMMIT APPROVED                            ║"
echo "╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝"

### 1. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:583caa5c` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

🚨 **BLOCKING: `kill()` prelude inverts the protected/unprotected logic for negative-pid (process-group) targets**

The `-[0-9]*)` branch of the generated `kill()` filter keeps and drops the opposite of what the positive-pid branch keeps and drops — and the opposite of what the dartdoc (line 47: *"filters … pids (and their `-pgid` group targets) out of the arguments"*) and the AGENTS.md contract claim.

Current logic (`lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart:55-64`):

```sh
-[0-9]*)
  __fa_n="${__fa_a#-}"
  __fa_keep=1
  ...
  if [ "$__fa_keep" = 1 ]; then
    __fa_hit=1            # UNPROTECTED group target: marked as "hit" …
  else
    __fa_rest="$__fa_rest $__fa_a"   # … PROTECTED group target: kept for the real kill
  fi
  ;;
```

Both failure modes reproduced live with the exact artifacts generated by `bashGuardPrelude()` (dummy = disposable `setsid sleep`):

1. **Protected group target is signaled.** `kill -TERM -<pgid>` with `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS='<pgid>'`: `__fa_keep=0` appends the arg to `__fa_rest`, no other arg sets `__fa_hit`, so the `__fa_hit = 0` fast path executes `command kill "$@"` **byte-identical** — the protected process group was killed (dummy verified dead). This is precisely the kill spelling agents use to reap `setsid` background jobs (`kill -- -$PID`), i.e. the exact hazard gh-1763 invariant 2 names: *"must not be able to terminate `fa` …, its process group, or its parent supervisor chain"*.
2. **Unprotected group kill is silently swallowed.** `kill -TERM -<pgid>` with no protected hit: `__fa_hit=1`, `__fa_pids_left=0` (only the positive branch increments it) → the real `kill` never runs, the function prints the false message `fa: kill skipped protected pid(s)` and returns **0** — the caller believes the group died; the dummy was still alive.

Fix: mirror the positive-pid branch (`keep=1` → append to `__fa_rest` **and** count it toward `__fa_pids_left`; `keep=0` → `__fa_hit=1`), so a mixed `kill -9 -<protected_pgid> <victim>` filters only the group target and still signals the victim. Please add the missing regression tests: `kill -- -PGID` in both polarities (protected → survives, unprotected → reaped) — the current suite only covers the positive-pid path, which is why this shipped green.

### 2. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:a1f81563` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

🚨 **BLOCKING: pkill shim forwards pgrep *output-mode* flags and then reads the output as a pid list — signals wrong targets**

The guarded path expands victims with `pids=$("$FA_REAL_PGREP" $sel "$@")` (line 150), but the only output-shape guard is the short-cluster `[cv]` check (line 125). Every *output-mode* flag slips past it and corrupts the victim set — all verified live on this host (procps-ng 4.0.4) with an instrumented copy of the exact shim `buildPkillShim()` generates:

1. **`--count` → signals an arbitrary unrelated pid.** Long options are never scanned by the `c`/`v` loop, so `--count` lands in `sel`. `pgrep --count` prints a bare *number*, the loop reads it as a pid: `pkill --count -f "sleep 99993"` (2 matches) produced `SHIM-WOULD-SIGNAL pid=3` — i.e. a real run SIGTERMs pid 3 and exits 0, while real `pkill -c` signals nothing.
2. **`-l` / `-a` → a usage error becomes a kill-everything.** Real `pkill -l` / `pkill -a` is invalid on procps 4.0.4 (`pkill: invalid option -- 'l'`, rc=2, signals nothing). The shim passes them to `pgrep`, gets `pid name` rows, cuts them to the pid column (line 158's comment even documents that shape) and signals **every match** — instrumented run confirmed it computed kill targets for `pkill -l -f <pat>` and `pkill -a -f <pat>`.

Fix suggestion: before the guarded path, `exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@"` when any argument is a long option other than `--signal`/`--signal=`, or a short cluster containing `l` or `a` in addition to `c`/`v` — the same honest-fallback rule the shim already applies elsewhere. Also update the stale line-158 comment (`pgrep -l rows are "pid name"` — the shim never passes `-l`; today the `cut` is a no-op, and it is exactly the mechanism that turns list output into kill targets when `-l`/`-a` *does* reach pgrep).

2. **Unprotected group kill is silently swallowed.** `kill -TERM -<pgid>` with no protected hit: `__fa_hit=1`, `__fa_pids_left=0` (only the positive branch increments it) → the real `kill` never runs, the function prints the false message `fa: kill skipped protected pid(s)` and returns **0** — the caller believes the group died; the dummy was still alive.

Fix: mirror the positive-pid branch (`keep=1` → append to `__fa_rest` **and** count it toward `__fa_pids_left`; `keep=0` → `__fa_hit=1`), so a mixed `kill -9 -<protected_pgid> <victim>` filters only the group target and still signals the victim. Please add the missing regression tests: `kill -- -PGID` in both polarities (protected → survives, unprotected → reaped) — the current suite only covers the positive-pid path, which is why this shipped green.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

🚨 **BLOCKING: pkill shim forwards pgrep *output-mode* flags and then reads the output as a pid list — signals wrong targets**

The guarded path expands victims with `pids=$("$FA_REAL_PGREP" $sel "$@")` (line 150), but the only output-shape guard is the short-cluster `[cv]` check (line 125). Every *output-mode* flag slips past it and corrupts the victim set — all verified live on this host (procps-ng 4.0.4) with an instrumented copy of the exact shim `buildPkillShim()` generates:

1. **`--count` → signals an arbitrary unrelated pid.** Long options are never scanned by the `c`/`v` loop, so `--count` lands in `sel`. `pgrep --count` prints a bare *number*, the loop reads it as a pid: `pkill --count -f "sleep 99993"` (2 matches) produced `SHIM-WOULD-SIGNAL pid=3` — i.e. a real run SIGTERMs pid 3 and exits 0, while real `pkill -c` signals nothing.
2. **`-l` / `-a` → a usage error becomes a kill-everything.** Real `pkill -l` / `pkill -a` is invalid on procps 4.0.4 (`pkill: invalid option -- 'l'`, rc=2, signals nothing). The shim passes them to `pgrep`, gets `pid name` rows, cuts them to the pid column (line 158's comment even documents that shape) and signals **every match** — instrumented run confirmed it computed kill targets for `pkill -l -f <pat>` and `pkill -a -f <pat>`.

Fix suggestion: before the guarded path, `exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@"` when any argument is a long option other than `--signal`/`--signal=`, or a short cluster containing `l` or `a` in addition to `c`/`v` — the same honest-fallback rule the shim already applies elsewhere. Also update the stale line-158 comment (`pgrep -l rows are "pid name"` — the shim never passes `-l`; today the `cut` is a no-op, and it is exactly the mechanism that turns list output into kill targets when `-l`/`-a` *does* reach pgrep).

Please pin both shapes in `bash_self_defense_test.dart`: `pkill --count -f <unique>` must not signal pid `<count>`, and `pkill -l -f <unique>` must not signal anything.

The dartdoc (line 99) lists `-u root` / `-t tty` as shapes "the shim does not model" → `exec` real `pkill`. Concretely: `pkill -u "$(id -u)" -f "dart "` — flag and value as separate argv items — makes the operand loop break at the value, `[ "$#" -ne 1 ]` fires, and the **unshimmed** real `pkill` runs; its `-f "dart "` match hits the harness cmdline and the session aborts (the exact gh-1746 run-39661276610 failure this PR closes). **ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

💡 **SUGGESTION: unchecked `chmod` — a silent failure bricks every `pkill` in the child**

`await Process.run('chmod', <String>['700', file.path]);` ignores the result. If it fails (noexec-mounted `$TMPDIR`, hardened `chmod` policy), the shims stay non-executable and every subsequent bash tool call that invokes `pkill`/`killall` dies with `Permission denied` instead of degrading to the real binary. Cheap hardening: check `exitCode` and drop the shim from the provision on failure (the guard already has the degrade-to-null pathway for exactly this class of failure).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --
  UNFORMATTED=$(dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed $STAGED_DART 2>/dev/null | grep '^Changed' || true)
  if [ -n "$UNFORMATTED" ]; then
    echo "❌ dart format could not fix these files (syntax error?):"
    echo "$UNFORMATTED"
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# THE shared fast gate (same script, same path filters as CI). --hook makes
# it derive the scope from the STAGED diff. It unsets GIT_* env itself
# after reading hook mode.
bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --hook

# Issue #447: crap4dart quality gates over the STAGED core diff
# (core-only #433 split — the flutter_app gates run in CI's
# app-crap-gate job). The root crap4dart.yaml enables exactly
# broken_goldens; `check --staged` no-ops when no Dart file is staged.
# Equivalent to the managed block `crap4dart install --force` would
# append — do not stack both. Requires crap4dart >= 0.9 (the gate
# framework; older pins only knew `analyze`).
if command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  C4D_VER=$(dart pub global list 2>/dev/null | awk '$1=="crap4dart"{print $2}')
  case "$C4D_VER" in
    # gh-1106: floor 0.11.0 — the root crap4dart.yaml duplication block
    # uses 0.11.0-only keys (ignore_locals/ignorable); the strict config
    # parser throws ConfigException on unknown keys, so older pins fail
    # rather than silently run without Type-2 detection.
    0.1[1-9].*|0.[2-9][0-9].*|[1-9].*)
      echo "🧪 crap4dart gates (staged core files)..."
      # gh-1106: --baseline — the Type-2 duplication gate ships with a
      # committed snapshot of pre-existing findings; hooks must flag only
      # NEW duplication, same contract as CI.
      if ! dart pub global run crap4dart check --staged --baseline; then
        echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — crap4dart gates" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      # Issue #1234 rework: the ≤2800 ceiling over test/ + example/ via
      # the loc-scope companion config (the package config's sources are
      # [lib, bin]; 0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override). No-ops
      # unless a staged file lives under test/ or example/.
      if ! dart pub global run crap4dart check --staged --config crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml --only loc; then
        echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — loc scope (test/example)" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      ;;
    "")
      ;; # not activated — skip silently (CI and the fast gate cover it)
    *)
      echo "⚠️  crap4dart $C4D_VER is too old for the gates (need >= 0.11.0);" \
           "skipping — run: dart pub global activate crap4dart '>=0.11.0 <0.12.0'" >&2
      ;;
  esac
fi

# Golden-coverage quick check — only when the staged diff can affect the
# flutter_app (the gate's own markers already told us the flutter stage
# ran or was skipped; recompute cheaply from the staged paths here).
STAGED=$(git diff --cached --name-only || true)
if echo "$STAGED" | grep -qE '^(flutter_app/|packages/|lib/|scripts/|\.github/|pubspec\.)' \
   || ! echo "$STAGED" | grep -qE '\.(md)$|^docs/|^prompts/'; then
  if command -v flutter >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "🔍 Checking golden coverage..."
    if python3 scripts/check_goldens.py --quick; then
      echo "✅ Golden gate OK"
    else
      exit 1
    fi
  fi
fi

# Issue #433 AC1 (cheap, config-only): README CRAP badge must equal the
# crap4dart.yaml thresholds — runs only when a config or the README is
# staged, i.e. exactly the files that can drift apart.
if echo "$STAGED" | grep -qE '(^|/)crap4dart\.yaml$|^README\.md$'; then
  python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py
fi

echo ""
echo "╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗"
echo "║  ✅ ALL QUALITY GATES PASSED — COMMIT APPROVED                            ║"
echo "╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝"

🚨 **BLOCKING: `kill()` prelude inverts the protected/unprotected logic for negative-pid (process-group) targets**

The `-[0-9]*)` branch of the generated `kill()` filter keeps and drops the opposite of what the positive-pid branch keeps and drops — and the opposite of what the dartdoc (line 47: *"filters … pids (and their `-pgid` group targets) out of the arguments"*) and the AGENTS.md contract claim.

Current logic (`lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart:55-64`):

```sh
-[0-9]*)
  __fa_n="${__fa_a#-}"
  __fa_keep=1
  ...
  if [ "$__fa_keep" = 1 ]; then
    __fa_hit=1            # UNPROTECTED group target: marked as "hit" …
  else
    __fa_rest="$__fa_rest $__fa_a"   # … PROTECTED group target: kept for the real kill
  fi
  ;;
```

Both failure modes reproduced live with the exact artifacts generated by `bashGuardPrelude()` (dummy = disposable `setsid sleep`):

1. **Protected group target is signaled.** `kill -TERM -<pgid>` with `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS='<pgid>'`: `__fa_keep=0` appends the arg to `__fa_rest`, no other arg sets `__fa_hit`, so the `__fa_hit = 0` fast path executes `command kill "$@"` **byte-identical** — the protected process group was killed (dummy verified dead). This is precisely the kill spelling agents use to reap `setsid` background jobs (`kill -- -$PID`), i.e. the exact hazard gh-1763 invariant 2 names: *"must not be able to terminate `fa` …, its process group, or its parent supervisor chain"*.
2. **Unprotected group kill is silently swallowed.** `kill -TERM -<pgid>` with no protected hit: `__fa_hit=1`, `__fa_pids_left=0` (only the positive branch increments it) → the real `kill` never runs, the function prints the false message `fa: kill skipped protected pid(s)` and returns **0** — the caller believes the group died; the dummy was still alive.

Fix: mirror the positive-pid branch (`keep=1` → append to `__fa_rest` **and** count it toward `__fa_pids_left`; `keep=0` → `__fa_hit=1`), so a mixed `kill -9 -<protected_pgid> <victim>` filters only the group target and still signals the victim. Please add the missing regression tests: `kill -- -PGID` in both polarities (protected → survives, unprotected → reaped) — the current suite only covers the positive-pid path, which is why this shipped green.

### 2. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:a1f81563` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

The guarded path expands victims with `pids=$("$FA_REAL_PGREP" $sel "$@")` (line 150), but the only output-shape guard is the short-cluster `[cv]` check (line 125). Every *output-mode* flag slips past it and corrupts the victim set — all verified live on this host (procps-ng 4.0.4) with an instrumented copy of the exact shim `buildPkillShim()` generates:

1. **`--count` → signals an arbitrary unrelated pid.** Long options are never scanned by the `c`/`v` loop, so `--count` lands in `sel`. `pgrep --count` prints a bare *number*, the loop reads it as a pid: `pkill --count -f "sleep 99993"` (2 matches) produced `SHIM-WOULD-SIGNAL pid=3` — i.e. a real run SIGTERMs pid 3 and exits 0, while real `pkill -c` signals nothing.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1777._

> ℹ️ **6 resolved thread(s) excluded; 11 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `kill()` prelude inverts the protected/unprotected logic for negative-pid (process-group) targets**

The `-[0-9]*)` branch of the generated `kill()` filter keeps and drops the opposite of what the positive-pid branch keeps and drops — and the opposite of what the dartdoc (line 47: *"filters … pids (and their `-pgid` group targets) out of the arguments"*) and the AGENTS.md contract claim.

Current logic (`lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart:55-64`):

```sh
-[0-9]*)
  __fa_n="${__fa_a#-}"
  __fa_keep=1
  ...
  if [ "$__fa_keep" = 1 ]; then
    __fa_hit=1            # UNPROTECTED group target: marked as "hit" …
  else
    __fa_rest="$__fa_rest $__fa_a"   # … PROTECTED group target: kept for the real kill
  fi
  ;;
```

Both failure modes reproduced live with the exact artifacts generated by `bashGuardPrelude()` (dummy = disposable `setsid sleep`):

1. **Protected group target is signaled.** `kill -TERM -<pgid>` with `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS='<pgid>'`: `__fa_keep=0` appends the arg to `__fa_rest`, no other arg sets `__fa_hit`, so the `__fa_hit = 0` fast path executes `command kill "$@"` **byte-identical** — the protected process group was killed (dummy verified dead). This is precisely the kill spelling agents use to reap `setsid` background jobs (`kill -- -$PID`), i.e. the exact hazard gh-1763 invariant 2 names: *"must not be able to terminate `fa` …, its process group, or its parent supervisor chain"*.
2. **Unprotected group kill is silently swallowed.** `kill -TERM -<pgid>` with no protected hit: `__fa_hit=1`, `__fa_pids_left=0` (only the positive branch increments it) → the real `kill` never runs, the function prints the false message `fa: kill skipped protected pid(s)` and returns **0** — the caller believes the group died; the dummy was still alive.

Fix: mirror the positive-pid branch (`keep=1` → append to `__fa_rest` **and** count it toward `__fa_pids_left`; `keep=0` → `__fa_hit=1`), so a mixed `kill -9 -<protected_pgid> <victim>` filters only the group target and still signals the victim. Please add the missing regression tests: `kill -- -PGID` in both polarities (protected → survives, unprotected → reaped) — the current suite only covers the positive-pid path, which is why this shipped green.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

🚨 **BLOCKING: pkill shim forwards pgrep *output-mode* flags and then reads the output as a pid list — signals wrong targets**

The guarded path expands victims with `pids=$("$FA_REAL_PGREP" $sel "$@")` (line 150), but the only output-shape guard is the short-cluster `[cv]` check (line 125). Every *output-mode* flag slips past it and corrupts the victim set — all verified live on this host (procps-ng 4.0.4) with an instrumented copy of the exact shim `buildPkillShim()` generates:

1. **`--count` → signals an arbitrary unrelated pid.** Long options are never scanned by the `c`/`v` loop, so `--count` lands in `sel`. `pgrep --count` prints a bare *number*, the loop reads it as a pid: `pkill --count -f "sleep 99993"` (2 matches) produced `SHIM-WOULD-SIGNAL pid=3` — i.e. a real run SIGTERMs pid 3 and exits 0, while real `pkill -c` signals nothing.
2. **`-l` / `-a` → a usage error becomes a kill-everything.** Real `pkill -l` / `pkill -a` is invalid on procps 4.0.4 (`pkill: invalid option -- 'l'`, rc=2, signals nothing). The shim passes them to `pgrep`, gets `pid name` rows, cuts them to the pid column (line 158's comment even documents that shape) and signals **every match** — instrumented run confirmed it computed kill targets for `pkill -l -f <pat>` and `pkill -a -f <pat>`.

Fix suggestion: before the guarded path, `exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@"` when any argument is a long option other than `--signal`/`--signal=`, or a short cluster containing `l` or `a` in addition to `c`/`v` — the same honest-fallback rule the shim already applies elsewhere. Also update the stale line-158 comment (`pgrep -l rows are "pid name"` — the shim never passes `-l`; today the `cut` is a no-op, and it is exactly the mechanism that turns list output into kill targets when `-l`/`-a` *does* reach pgrep).

Please pin both shapes in `bash_self_defense_test.dart`: `pkill --count -f <unique>` must not signal pid `<count>`, and `pkill -l -f <unique>` must not signal anything.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

🚨 **BLOCKING: still in conflict with `main` — merge fails today**

Verified against `origin/main` (`a8393dc21e`, which advanced ~2h after this branch's `d6d5824` merge):

```
git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD
→ CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in CHANGELOG.md
```

Both sides appended an entry under `## Unreleased` again (this PR's `fix(gh-1763)` vs main's `fix(gh-1745)` / `feat(#1750)` entries from #1765/#1768). Same shape as the previous conflict round: keep both entries in the file's newest-first order and push — validation re-runs automatically.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: split-form selection values still reach the *real* `pkill`, which can kill the harness — the original gh-1763 crash shape**

The dartdoc (line 99) lists `-u root` / `-t tty` as shapes "the shim does not model" → `exec` real `pkill`. Concretely: `pkill -u "$(id -u)" -f "dart "` — flag and value as separate argv items — makes the operand loop break at the value, `[ "$#" -ne 1 ]` fires, and the **unshimmed** real `pkill` runs; its `-f "dart "` match hits the harness cmdline and the session aborts (the exact gh-1746 run-39661276610 failure this PR closes). Same for `-t tty1`, `-s 1`, `-F pidfile`, `-P ppid` written space-separated (the glued forms, `-urot`, work).

Two questions before merge:

1. Is silently degrading to *no harness protection* for these spellings acceptable, or should the arg loop consume a value for the known value-taking selection flags (`-u -U -g -s -t -P -G -r -O -q -F`) so the guarded path still runs?
2. Either way, the AGENTS.md contract added in this PR says the guard excludes the harness chain "while legitimate victims stay killable" without mentioning this residual — please carry the caveat there (one sentence), since AGENTS.md is what future agents will treat as the guarantee.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

💡 **SUGGESTION: this PATH assertion requires a procps host (pkill/pgrep installed)**

`expect(parts.first, contains('fa_sh_guard_'))` only holds when `provisionBashGuard()` produced a shim dir — i.e. when the host has `pgrep` (see `_buildShimScripts`, which returns `const {}` without it). On a minimal container without procps the shim dir is null and `parts.first` is `/bin`, failing this test. Every gh-1763 test in `bash_self_defense_test.dart` guards this with `skip: Platform.isWindows ? …`, but that doesn't cover a Linux host without procps (docker-slim CI images, distroless). Suggest `skip:`-guarding on a `command -v pgrep` probe, or asserting only `parts, contains('/bin')`.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

💡 **SUGGESTION: unchecked `chmod` — a silent failure bricks every `pkill` in the child**

`await Process.run('chmod', <String>['700', file.path]);` ignores the result. If it fails (noexec-mounted `$TMPDIR`, hardened `chmod` policy), the shims stay non-executable and every subsequent bash tool call that invokes `pkill`/`killall` dies with `Permission denied` instead of degrading to the real binary. Cheap hardening: check `exitCode` and drop the shim from the provision on failure (the guard already has the degrade-to-null pathway for exactly this class of failure).

armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics. Self-signal immunity
  (gh-1763): POSIX scripts are delivered from a per-exec private temp
  file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — prelude restores `sh -c`
  positional-param parity, so `$0`/`$#`/exit codes/`set -e`/stdin are
  unchanged; legacy `sh -c <command>` fallback when the temp dir cannot
  be created) so the wrapper argv never carries the script body —
  `pkill -f <pat>` inside a command cannot match its own shell; a
  provisioned-once guard (`lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`) puts
  `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims at the head of PATH plus a `kill()`
  prelude function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`, overridable per exec via
  `ShellExecOptions.env` for tests) and the invoking shell, while
  legitimate victims stay killable; Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
  Residual caveat: shapes the shim cannot model — output modes
  (`-c`, `-v`, `-l`, `-a`, `--count`, any other long option), a signal
  spelled after the pattern, extra operands, or a selection pgrep
  rejects — exec the real, unshimed binary and are NOT covered by the
  exemption (keep the pattern away from the harness cmdline in those
  spellings).
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.

- fix(gh-1763): a `bash` tool command running broad process kills can no
  longer signal its own shell or the harness. Scripts are delivered from a
  per-exec private temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>`) so the wrapper
  argv never carries the script body (`pkill -f <pattern>` cannot
  self-match its own `sh -c`; `$0`/`$#`/exit codes/`set -e`/stdin stay
  identical), a PATH shim for `pkill`/`killall` plus a `kill()` prelude
  guard exempt the harness pid chain + process group (exported as
  `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell from the child's own kills
  while legitimate victims (stuck test runners, background servers) are
  still terminated, and headless `SIGTERM` aborts now log
  `fa: SIGTERM received …` so a child-issued kill never masquerades as a
  user Ctrl+C (exit code contract unchanged: 130 graceful, 143 escalate).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit mu…

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --
  UNFORMATTED=$(dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed $STAGED_DART 2>/dev/null | grep '^Changed' || true)
  if [ -n "$UNFORMATTED" ]; then
    echo "❌ dart format could not fix these files (syntax error?):"
    echo "$UNFORMATTED"
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# THE shared fast gate (same script, same path filters as CI). --hook makes
# it derive the scope from the STAGED diff. It unsets GIT_* env itself
# after reading hook mode.
bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --hook

# Issue #447: crap4dart quality gates over the STAGED core diff
# (core-only #433 split — the flutter_app gates run in CI's
# app-crap-gate job). The root crap4dart.yaml enables exactly
# broken_goldens; `check --staged` no-ops when no Dart file is staged.
# Equivalent to the managed block `crap4dart install --force` would
# append — do not stack both. Requires crap4dart >= 0.9 (the gate
# framework; older pins only knew `analyze`).
if command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  C4D_VER=$(dart pub global list 2>/dev/null | awk '$1=="crap4dart"{print $2}')
  case "$C4D_VER" in
    # gh-1106: floor 0.11.0 — the root crap4dart.yaml duplication block
    # uses 0.11.0-only keys (ignore_locals/ignorable); the strict config
    # parser throws ConfigException on unknown keys, so older pins fail
    # rather than silently run without Type-2 detection.
    0.1[1-9].*|0.[2-9][0-9].*|[1-9].*)
      echo "🧪 crap4dart gates (staged core files)..."
      # gh-1106: --baseline — the Type-2 duplication gate ships with a
      # committed snapshot of pre-existing findings; hooks must flag only
      # NEW duplication, same contract as CI.
      if ! dart pub global run crap4dart check --staged --baseline; then
        echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — crap4dart gates" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      # Issue #1234 rework: the ≤2800 ceiling over test/ + example/ via
      # the loc-scope companion config (the package config's sources are
      # [lib, bin]; 0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override). No-ops
      # unless a staged file lives under test/ or example/.
      if ! dart pub global run crap4dart check --staged --config crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml --only loc; then
        echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — loc scope (test/example)" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      ;;
    "")
      ;; # not activated — skip silently (CI and the fast gate cover it)
    *)
      echo "⚠️  crap4dart $C4D_VER is too old for the gates (need >= 0.11.0);" \
           "skipping — run: dart pub global activate crap4dart '>=0.11.0 <0.12.0'" >&2
      ;;
  esac
fi

# Golden-coverage quick check — only when the staged diff can affect the
# flutter_app (the gate's own markers already told us the flutter stage
# ran or was skipped; recompute cheaply from the staged paths here).
STAGED=$(git diff --cached --name-only || true)
if echo "$STAGED" | grep -qE '^(flutter_app/|packages/|lib/|scripts/|\.github/|pubspec\.)' \
   || ! echo "$STAGED" | grep -qE '\.(md)$|^docs/|^prompts/'; then
  if command -v flutter >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "🔍 Checking golden coverage..."
    if python3 scripts/check_goldens.py --quick; then
      echo "✅ Golden gate OK"
    else
      exit 1
    fi
  fi
fi

# Issue #433 AC1 (cheap, config-only): README CRAP badge must equal the
# crap4dart.yaml thresholds — runs only when a config or the README is
# staged, i.e. exactly the files that can drift apart.
if echo "$STAGED" | grep -qE '(^|/)crap4dart\.yaml$|^README\.md$'; then
  python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py
fi

echo ""
echo "╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗"
echo "║  ✅ ALL QUALITY GATES PASSED — COMMIT APPROVED                            ║"
echo "╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝"

The `-[0-9]*)` branch of the generated `kill()` filter keeps and drops the opposite of what the positive-pid branch keeps and drops — and the opposite of what the dartdoc (line 47: *"filters … pids (and their `-pgid` group targets) out of the arguments"*) and the AGENTS.md contract claim.

Current logic (`lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart:55-64`):

```sh
-[0-9]*)
  __fa_n="${__fa_a#-}"
  __fa_keep=1
  ...
  if [ "$__fa_keep" = 1 ]; then
    __fa_hit=1            # UNPROTECTED group target: marked as "hit" …

The dartdoc (line 99) lists `-u root` / `-t tty` as shapes "the shim does not model" → `exec` real `pkill`. Concretely: `pkill -u "$(id -u)" -f "dart "` — flag and value as separate argv items — makes the operand loop break at the value, `[ "$#" -ne 1 ]` fires, and the **unshimmed** real `pkill` runs; its `-f "dart "` match hits the harness cmdline and the session aborts (the exact gh-1746 run-39661276610 failure this PR closes). Same for `-t tty1`, `-s 1`, `-F pidfile`, `-P ppid` written space-separated (the glued forms, `-urot`, work).

2. Either way, the AGENTS.md contract added in this PR says the guard excludes the harness chain "while legitimate victims stay killable" without mentioning this residual — please carry the caveat there (one sentence), since AGENTS.md is what future agents will treat as the guarantee.

💡 **SUGGESTION: this PATH assertion requires a procps host (pkill/pgrep installed)**

`expect(parts.first, contains('fa_sh_guard_'))` only holds when `provisionBashGuard()` produced a shim dir — i.e. when the host has `pgrep` (see `_buildShimScripts`, which returns `const {}` without it). On a minimal container without procps the shim dir is null and `parts.first` is `/bin`, failing this test. Every gh-1763 test in `bash_self_defense_test.dart` guards this with `skip: Platform.isWindows ? …`, but that doesn't cover a Linux host without procps (docker-slim CI images, distroless). Suggest `skip:`-guarding on a `command -v pgrep` probe, or asserting only `parts, contains('/bin')`.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):

💡 **SUGGESTION: unchecked `chmod` — a silent failure bricks every `pkill` in the child**

`await Process.run('chmod', <String>['700', file.path]);` ignores the result. If it fails (noexec-mounted `$TMPDIR`, hardened `chmod` policy), the shims stay non-executable and every subsequent bash tool call that invokes `pkill`/`killall` dies with `Permission denied` instead of degrading to the real binary. Cheap hardening: check `exitCode` and drop the shim from the provision on failure (the guard already has the degrade-to-null pathway for exactly this class of failure).

blocks.text:
armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics. Self-signal immunity
  (gh-1763): POSIX scripts are delivered from a per-exec private temp
  file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — prelude restores `sh -c`
  positional-param parity, so `$0`/`$#`/exit codes/`set -e`/stdin are
  unchanged; legacy `sh -c <command>` fallback when the temp dir cannot
  be created) so the wrapper argv never carries the script body —
  `pkill -f <pat>` inside a command cannot match its own shell; a
  provisioned-once guard (`lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`) puts
  `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims at the head of PATH plus a `kill()`
  prelude function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --
  UNFORMATTED=$(dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed $STAGED_DART 2>/dev/null | grep '^Changed' || true)
  if [ -n "$UNFORMATTED" ]; then
    echo "❌ dart format could not fix these files (syntax error?):"
    echo "$UNFORMATTED"
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# THE shared fast gate (same script, same path filters as CI). --hook makes
# it derive the scope from the STAGED diff. It unsets GIT_* env itself
# after reading hook mode.
bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --hook

# Issue #447: crap4dart quality gates over the STAGED core diff
# (core-only #433 split — the flutter_app gates run in CI's
# app-crap-gate job). The root crap4dart.yaml enables exactly
# broken_goldens; `check --staged` no-ops when no Dart file is staged.
# Equivalent to the managed block `crap4dart install --force` would
# append — do not stack both. Requires crap4dart >= 0.9 (the gate
# framework; older pins only knew `analyze`).
if command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  C4D_VER=$(dart pub global list 2>/dev/null | awk '$1=="crap4dart"{print $2}')
  case "$C4D_VER" in
    # gh-1106: floor 0.11.0 — the root crap4dart.yaml duplication block
    # uses 0.11.0-only keys (ignore_locals/ignorable); the strict config
    # parser throws ConfigException on unknown keys, so older pins fail
    # rather than silently run without Type-2 detection.
    0.1[1-9].*|0.[2-9][0-9].*|[1-9].*)
      echo "🧪 crap4dart gates (staged core files)..."
      # gh-1106: --baseline — the Type-2 duplication gate ships with a
      # committed snapshot of pre-existing findings; hooks must flag only
      # NEW duplication, same contract as CI.
      if ! dart pub global run crap4dart check --staged --baseline; then
        echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — crap4dart gates" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      # Issue #1234 rework: the ≤2800 ceiling over test/ + example/ via
      # the loc-scope companion config (the package config's sources are
      # [lib, bin]; 0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override). No-ops
      # unless a staged file lives under test/ or example/.
      if ! dart pub global run crap4dart check --staged --config crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml --only loc; then
        echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — loc scope (test/example)" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      ;;
    "")
      ;; # not activated — skip silently (CI and the fast gate cover it)
    *)
      echo "⚠️  crap4dart $C4D_VER is too old for the gates (need >= 0.11.0);" \
           "skipping — run: dart pub global activate crap4dart '>=0.11.0 <0.12.0'" >&2
      ;;
  esac
fi

# Golden-coverage quick check — only when the staged diff can affect the
# flutter_app (the gate's own markers already told us the flutter stage

STAGED=$(git diff --cached --name-only || true)
if echo "$STAGED" | grep -qE '^(flutter_app/|packages/|lib/|scripts/|\.github/|pubspec\.)' \
   || ! echo "$STAGED" | grep -qE '\.(md)$|^docs/|^prompts/'; then

    fi

fi

# crap4dart.yaml thresholds — runs only when a config or the README is

fi

### 1. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:583caa5c` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

🚨 **BLOCKING: `kill()` prelude inverts the protected/unprotected logic for negative-pid (process-group) targets**

The `-[0-9]*)` branch of the generated `kill()` filter keeps and drops the opposite of what the positive-pid branch keeps and drops — and the opposite of what the dartdoc (line 47: *"filters … pids (and their `-pgid` group targets) out of the arguments"*) and the AGENTS.md contract claim.

Current logic (`lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart:55-64`):

```sh
-[0-9]*)
  __fa_n="${__fa_a#-}"
  __fa_keep=1
  ...
  if [ "$__fa_keep" = 1 ]; then
    __fa_hit=1            # UNPROTECTED group target: marked as "hit" …
  else
    __fa_rest="$__fa_rest $__fa_a"   # … PROTECTED group target: kept for the real kill
  fi
  ;;
```

Both failure modes reproduced live with the exact artifacts generated by `bashGuardPrelude()` (dummy = disposable `setsid sleep`):

1. **Protected group target is signaled.** `kill -TERM -<pgid>` with `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS='<pgid>'`: `__fa_keep=0` appends the arg to `__fa_rest`, no other arg sets `__fa_hit`, so the `__fa_hit = 0` fast path executes `command kill "$@"` **byte-identical** — the protected process group was killed (dummy verified dead). This is precisely the kill spelling agents use to reap `setsid` background jobs (`kill -- -$PID`), i.e. the exact hazard gh-1763 invariant 2 names: *"must not be able to terminate `fa` …, its process group, or its parent supervisor chain"*.
2. **Unprotected group kill is silently swallowed.** `kill -TERM -<pgid>` with no protected hit: `__fa_hit=1`, `__fa_pids_left=0` (only the positive branch increments it) → the real `kill` never runs, the function prints the false message `fa: kill skipped protected pid(s)` and returns **0** — the caller believes the group died; the dummy was still alive.

Fix: mirror the positive-pid branch (`keep=1` → append to `__fa_rest` **and** count it toward `__fa_pids_left`; `keep=0` → `__fa_hit=1`), so a mixed `kill -9 -<protected_pgid> <victim>` filters only the group target and still signals the victim. Please add the missing regression tests: `kill -- -PGID` in both polarities (protected → survives, unprotected → reaped) — the current suite only covers the positive-pid path, which is why this shipped green.

### 2. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:a1f81563` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

🚨 **BLOCKING: pkill shim forwards pgrep *output-mode* flags and then reads the output as a pid list — signals wrong targets**

The guarded path expands victims with `pids=$("$FA_REAL_PGREP" $sel "$@")` (line 150), but the only output-shape guard is the short-cluster `[cv]` check (line 125). Every *output-mode* flag slips past it and corrupts the victim set — all verified live on this host (procps-ng 4.0.4) with an instrumented copy of the exact shim `buildPkillShim()` generates:

1. **`--count` → signals an arbitrary unrelated pid.** Long options are never scanned by the `c`/`v` loop, so `--count` lands in `sel`. `pgrep --count` prints a bare *number*, the loop reads it as a pid: `pkill --count -f "sleep 99993"` (2 matches) produced `SHIM-WOULD-SIGNAL pid=3` — i.e. a real run SIGTERMs pid 3 and exits 0, while real `pkill -c` signals nothing.
2. **`-l` / `-a` → a usage error becomes a kill-everything.** Real `pkill -l` / `pkill -a` is invalid on procps 4.0.4 (`pkill: invalid option -- 'l'`, rc=2, signals nothing). The shim passes them to `pgrep`, gets `pid name` rows, cuts them to the pid column (line 158's comment even documents that shape) and signals **every match** — instrumented run confirmed it computed kill targets for `pkill -l -f <pat>` and `pkill -a -f <pat>`.

Fix suggestion: before the guarded path, `exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@"` when any argument is a long option other than `--signal`/`--signal=`, or a short cluster containing `l` or `a` in addition to `c`/`v` — the same honest-fallback rule the shim already applies elsewhere. Also update the stale line-158 comment (`pgrep -l rows are "pid name"` — the shim never passes `-l`; today the `cut` is a no-op, and it is exactly the mechanism that turns list output into kill targets when `-l`/`-a` *does* reach pgrep).

Please pin both shapes in `bash_self_defense_test.dart`: `pkill --count -f <unique>` must not signal pid `<count>`, and `pkill -l -f <unique>` must not signal anything.

Current logic (`lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart:55-64`):

```sh
-[0-9]*)
  __fa_n="${__fa_a#-}"
  __fa_keep=1
  ...
  if [ "$__fa_keep" = 1 ]; then
    __fa_hit=1            # UNPROTECTED group target: marked as "hit" …
  else
    __fa_rest="$__fa_rest $__fa_a"   # … PROTECTED group target: kept for the real kill
  fi
  ;;
```

Both failure modes reproduced live with the exact artifacts generated by `bashGuardPrelude()` (dummy = disposable `setsid sleep`):

1. **Protected group target is signaled.** `kill -TERM -<pgid>` with `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS='<pgid>'`: `__fa_keep=0` appends the arg to `__fa_rest`, no other arg sets `__fa_hit`, so the `__fa_hit = 0` fast path executes `command kill "$@"` **byte-identical** — the protected process group was killed (dummy verified dead). This is precisely the kill spelling agents use to reap `setsid` background jobs (`kill -- -$PID`), i.e. the exact hazard gh-1763 invariant 2 names: *"must not be able to terminate `fa` …, its process group, or its parent supervisor chain"*.

blocks.text:
armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics. Self-signal immunity
  (gh-1763): POSIX scripts are delivered from a per-exec private temp
  file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — prelude restores `sh -c`
  positional-param parity, so `$0`/`$#`/exit codes/`set -e`/stdin are
  unchanged; legacy `sh -c <command>` fallback when the temp dir cannot
  be created) so the wrapper argv never carries the script body —
  `pkill -f <pat>` inside a command cannot match its own shell; a
  provisioned-once guard (`lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`) puts
  `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims at the head of PATH plus a `kill()`
  prelude function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`, overridable per exec via
  `ShellExecOptions.env` for tests) and the invoking shell, while
  legitimate victims stay killable; Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
  Residual caveat: shapes the shim cannot model — output modes
  (`-c`, `-v`, `-l`, `-a`, `--count`, any other long option), a signal
  spelled after the pattern, extra operands, or a selection pgrep
  rejects — exec the real, unshimed binary and are NOT covered by the
  exemption (keep the pattern away from the harness cmdline in those
  spellings).
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.

### 1. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:583caa5c` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

🚨 **BLOCKING: `kill()` prelude inverts the protected/unprotected logic for negative-pid (process-group) targets**

The `-[0-9]*)` branch of the generated `kill()` filter keeps and drops the opposite of what the positive-pid branch keeps and drops — and the opposite of what the dartdoc (line 47: *"filters … pids (and their `-pgid` group targets) out of the arguments"*) and the AGENTS.md contract claim.

Current logic (`lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart:55-64`):

```sh
-[0-9]*)
  __fa_n="${__fa_a#-}"
  __fa_keep=1
  ...
  if [ "$__fa_keep" = 1 ]; then
    __fa_hit=1            # UNPROTECTED group target: marked as "hit" …
  else
    __fa_rest="$__fa_rest $__fa_a"   # … PROTECTED group target: kept for the real kill
  fi
  ;;
```

Both failure modes reproduced live with the exact artifacts generated by `bashGuardPrelude()` (dummy = disposable `setsid sleep`):

1. **Protected group target is signaled.** `kill -TERM -<pgid>` with `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS='<pgid>'`: `__fa_keep=0` appends the arg to `__fa_rest`, no other arg sets `__fa_hit`, so the `__fa_hit = 0` fast path executes `command kill "$@"` **byte-identical** — the protected process group was killed (dummy verified dead). This is precisely the kill spelling agents use to reap `setsid` background jobs (`kill -- -$PID`), i.e. the exact hazard gh-1763 invariant 2 names: *"must not be able to terminate `fa` …, its process group, or its parent supervisor chain"*.
2. **Unprotected group kill is silently swallowed.** `kill -TERM -<pgid>` with no protected hit: `__fa_hit=1`, `__fa_pids_left=0` (only the positive branch increments it) → the real `kill` never runs, the function prints the false message `fa: kill skipped protected pid(s)` and returns **0** — the caller believes the group died; the dummy was still alive.

Fix: mirror the positive-pid branch (`keep=1` → append to `__fa_rest` **and** count it toward `__fa_pids_left`; `keep=0` → `__fa_hit=1`), so a mixed `kill -9 -<protected_pgid> <victim>` filters only the group target and still signals the victim. Please add the missing regression tests: `kill -- -PGID` in both polarities (protected → survives, unprotected → reaped) — the current suite only covers the positive-pid path, which is why this shipped green.

### 2. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:a1f81563` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

🚨 **BLOCKING: pkill shim forwards pgrep *output-mode* flags and then reads the output as a pid list — signals wrong targets**

The guarded path expands victims with `pids=$("$FA_REAL_PGREP" $sel "$@")` (line 150), but the only output-shape guard is the short-cluster `[cv]` check (line 125). Every *output-mode* flag slips past it and corrupts the victim set — all verified live on this host (procps-ng 4.0.4) with an instrumented copy of the exact shim `buildPkillShim()` generates:

1. **`--count` → signals an arbitrary unrelated pid.** Long options are never scanned by the `c`/`v` loop, so `--count` lands in `sel`. `pgrep --count` prints a bare *number*, the loop reads it as a pid: `pkill --count -f "sleep 99993"` (2 matches) produced `SHIM-WOULD-SIGNAL pid=3` — i.e. a real run SIGTERMs pid 3 and exits 0, while real `pkill -c` signals nothing.
2. **`-l` / `-a` → a usage error becomes a kill-everything.** Real `pkill -l` / `pkill -a` is invalid on procps 4.0.4 (`pkill: invalid option -- 'l'`, rc=2, signals nothing). The shim passes them to `pgrep`, gets `pid name` rows, cuts them to the pid column (line 158's comment even documents that shape) and signals **every match** — instrumented run confirmed it computed kill targets for `pkill -l -f <pat>` and `pkill -a -f <pat>`.

Fix suggestion: before the guarded path, `exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@"` when any argument is a long option other than `--signal`/`--signal=`, or a short cluster containing `l` or `a` in addition to `c`/`v` — the same honest-fallback rule the shim already applies elsewhere. Also update the stale line-158 comment (`pgrep -l rows are "pid name"` — the shim never passes `-l`; today the `cut` is a no-op, and it is exactly the mechanism that turns list output into kill targets when `-l`/`-a` *does* reach pgrep).

Please pin both shapes in `bash_self_defense_test.dart`: `pkill --count -f <unique>` must not signal pid `<count>`, and `pkill -l -f <unique>` must not signal anything.

  target, so it passes through uncounted. Without that, `kill -9 4242` with
